ORIGIN.quote: Thousands of labels are not thousands of authenticated agents; rotating truncated IP prefixes do not establish a botnet or vendor. Self-identification with OpenAI is suggestive, not model provenance.
ORIGIN.reason: A reader does learn, in one clause of the closing attribution-limits paragraph, that agents self-identified with OpenAI, but the report immediately discounts it as unauthenticated labelling that cannot establish provenance or vendor, so the takeaway is that the report declines to treat OpenAI origin as a live hypothesis. That explicit raise-then-set-aside puts it above the 0.2 band (where OpenAI-bearing artifacts like `AgentNEWTESTBYOPENAI456` and `OpenAIOct22CVD` appear only as unremarked page keys) but below 0.6, since OpenAI is never left standing as a possibility on the table.
